description.content:
Registration, login, session lookup and email verification.

### Email verification rule (important)

The register controller only sends a verification email when the request body contains `role: "customer"` **explicitly**.

| Body `role` | `isEmailVerified` | Verification email | Can log in immediately? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `"customer"` | `false` | Sent | No — verify first |
| `"admin"` | `true` | Not sent | Yes |
| omitted | `true` (role still defaults to `customer`) | Not sent | Yes |

So for quick local testing, omit `role` and you get a usable customer account with no SMTP round-trip.

Creates a **customer** account and emails a verification link.

`Public` — no token required.

### Body

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | ✅ | Trimmed |
| `email` | string | ✅ | Unique, lowercased, must match `x@y.z` |
| `password` | string | ✅ | Min 6 chars, hashed with bcrypt before saving |
| `role` | `customer` \| `admin` | ❌ | Defaults to `customer` |
| `phone` | string | ❌ | **Unique** across users — reuse causes a duplicate-key error |
| `address` | object | ❌ | `street`, `city`, `state`, `zip`, `country` |

### Responses

**201 Created**
```json
{
  "message": "User registered successfully. Please verify your email to activate your account.",
  "user": {
    "id": "66f0...",
    "name": "Ali Haider",
    "email": "customer@example.com",
    "role": "customer",
    "isEmailVerified": false
  }
}
```

**400 Bad Request** — `{ "message": "Name, email and password are required" }` or `{ "message": "User already exists" }`

### Notes

- Because `role` is `customer` here, login stays blocked with `403` until the email is verified.
- If SMTP vars (`EMAIL_HOST`, `EMAIL_USER`, `EMAIL_PASS`) are missing, the account is still created but no mail goes out — a warning is logged. Grab the token straight from the `emailVerificationToken` field in MongoDB in that case.

description.content:
Bootstraps an **admin** account. Same endpoint as customer registration, but `role: "admin"` marks the account as verified immediately, so you can log in right away.

`Public` — no token required. Use this once per fresh database, then rely on **Users → Create User** for further accounts.

### Responses

**201 Created**
```json
{
  "message": "User registered successfully.",
  "user": {
    "id": "66f0...",
    "name": "Admin User",
    "email": "admin@example.com",
    "role": "admin"
  }
}
```

`isEmailVerified` is omitted from the response for non-customer roles, but is stored as `true`.

Exchanges email + password for a JWT.

`Public` — no token required.

> **This is the request that powers the whole collection.** Its test script writes `token`, `user_id` and `user_role` into the active environment, so run it first.

### Body

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | ✅ |
| `password` | string | ✅ |

### Responses

**200 OK**
```json
{
  "message": "Login successfully",
  "token": "<your-jwt-token-here>",
  "user": {
    "id": "66f0...",
    "name": "Admin User",
    "email": "admin@example.com",
    "role": "admin",
    "isEmailVerified": true
  }
}
```

| Status | Body | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `Email and password are required` | Missing field |
| `401` | `Invalid email or password` | Wrong credentials (same message for unknown email — deliberate) |
| `403` | `Please verify your email before logging in` | `isEmailVerified` is `false` |

### Cookie

The response also sets an **httpOnly** cookie:

```
Set-Cookie: token=<jwt>; Max-Age=604800; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
```

Postman stores it automatically (see the **Cookies** link under Send), so subsequent requests carry it. Browser clients must opt in — `credentials: "include"` with fetch, or `withCredentials: true` with axios.

The cookie is `secure` + `SameSite=None` when `NODE_ENV=production`, and `SameSite=Lax` in development.

description.content:
Returns the full user document for whoever owns `{{token}}`.

`🔒 Authenticated` — any role.

### Responses

**200 OK**
```json
{
  "_id": "66f0...",
  "name": "Admin User",
  "email": "admin@example.com",
  "role": "admin",
  "address": { "city": "Karachi", "country": "Pakistan" },
  "phone": "03009999999",
  "isEmailVerified": true,
  "createdAt": "2026-08-06T10:15:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-08-06T10:15:00.000Z"
}
```

| Status | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `401` | `Authentication required` (no `Bearer` header), `Invalid token`, or `Token expired` |
| `404` | Token is valid but the user was deleted |

Flips `isEmailVerified` to `true` and clears the stored token.

`Public` — no auth header; the query-string token *is* the credential.

### Query params

| Param | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | ✅ | Signed JWT sent in the verification email. Valid for **24 hours**. |

### How to get the token locally

The email links to `FRONTEND_URL/verify-email?token=...`. Two ways to grab it without a frontend:

1. Open the email and copy the `token` query param out of the link.
2. No SMTP configured? Read it straight from Mongo:
   ```js
   db.users.findOne({ email: "customer@example.com" }, { emailVerificationToken: 1 })
   ```

Paste it into the `verification_token` environment variable and send.

### Responses

| Status | Body |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | `{ "message": "Email verified successfully" }` |
| `400` | `Verification token is required` / `Invalid or expired verification token` / `Verification token has expired` |

The endpoint is single-use: the token is nulled after success, so a second call returns `400`.
The JWT from the verification email link (24 h expiry).

### Path params

item.name: Get All Products (search, filter, sort, paginate)

description.content:
Lists active products with full query support.

`🌍 Public`

### Query parameters

| Param | Example | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | `2` | Page number (min `1`, default `1`) |
| `limit` | `20` | Page size (default `10`, **max `100`**) |
| `sort` | `-price`, `category,-price` | Multi-field sort; `-` = descending. Default `-createdAt` |
| `fields` | `name,price` / `-description,-images` | Include or exclude fields |
| `search` | `laptop` | Case-insensitive regex over `name` and `description` |
| `<field>` | `category=66f1...` | Exact-match filter on any schema field |
| `<field>[gte\|gt\|lte\|lt\|ne]` | `price[gte]=100` | Range / comparison filter |
| `<field>[in]` | `status[in]=a,b` | `$in` — comma-separated |
| `<field>[nin]` | `status[nin]=a,b` | `$nin` — comma-separated |

Combine freely: `?search=phone&price[gte]=200&price[lte]=800&sort=price&page=1&limit=5`

### Response — 200 OK
```json
{
  "message": "Products fetched successfully.",
  "data": [
    {
      "_id": "66f2...",
      "name": "Gaming Laptop",
      "description": "16GB RAM, RTX 4060",
      "price": 1499.99,
      "category": { "_id": "66f1...", "name": "Electronics", "slug": "electronics" },
      "stock": 12,
      "images": ["/uploads/66f2a1....png"],
      "sku": "LAP-001",
      "isActive": true,
      "createdAt": "2026-08-06T10:25:00.000Z"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "total": 42,
    "page": 1,
    "limit": 10,
    "totalPages": 5,
    "hasNextPage": true,
    "hasPrevPage": false
  }
}
```

### Security notes

- Keys starting with `$` are stripped from filters, so NoSQL operator injection through query params is blocked.
- Regex metacharacters in `search` are escaped (ReDoS protection).
- `isActive: true` is forced server-side and cannot be overridden by the client.
Page number. Min 1. Default 1.
Page size. Default 10, hard cap 100.
Comma-separated fields. Prefix with '-' for descending. Default '-createdAt'.
Case-insensitive regex across name and description.
Whitelist fields, or exclude with '-description,-images'.
Exact-match filter on any schema field.
Range filter — becomes $gte.
Range filter — becomes $lte.

Customer orders. **Every** route requires a token.

| Method | Path | Access |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/orders` | authenticated — admin sees all, customer sees own |
| `GET` | `/api/orders/:id` | authenticated — ownership checked |
| `POST` | `/api/orders` | authenticated |
| `PATCH` | `/api/orders/:id` | authenticated — ownership checked |
| `DELETE` | `/api/orders/:id` | authenticated |

### Status values

| Field | Allowed values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `pending`, `processing`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled` | `pending` |
| `paymentMethod` | `card`, `cod`, `paypal` | `cod` |
| `paymentStatus` | `pending`, `paid`, `failed`, `refunded` | `pending` |

Lists orders, scoped by role.

`🔒 Authenticated`

- **admin** → every order in the system
- **customer** → only orders where `user` matches the token's id

Returns a bare array (no pagination wrapper) with `user` populated as `{ name, email }` and each `items.product` as `{ name, price }`.

**200 OK**
```json
[
  {
    "_id": "66f3...",
    "user": { "_id": "66f0...", "name": "Ali Haider", "email": "customer@example.com" },
    "items": [
      { "product": { "_id": "66f2...", "name": "Gaming Laptop", "price": 1499.99 }, "quantity": 1, "price": 1499.99 }
    ],
    "totalAmount": 1499.99,
    "status": "pending",
    "paymentMethod": "cod",
    "paymentStatus": "pending",
    "shippingAddress": { "street": "12 Main Street", "city": "Karachi", "country": "Pakistan" },
    "createdAt": "2026-08-06T10:30:00.000Z"
  }
]
```

Fetches one order with `user` and `items.product` populated.

`🔒 Authenticated` — admins can read any order; customers only their own.

| Status | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | Order document |
| `403` | `Forbidden` — ownership check failed |
| `404` | `Order not found` |

> **Known issue:** the ownership check compares the *populated* `user` document against the token id, so it never matches for a customer and returns `403` even on their own order. Admins are unaffected. Fix by populating after the check, or by comparing `order.user._id.toString()`.

Places an order for the logged-in user.

`🔒 Authenticated`

### Body

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | array | ✅ | At least one entry |
| `items[].product` | ObjectId | ✅ | |
| `items[].quantity` | number | ✅ | Min `1` |
| `items[].price` | number | ✅ | Unit price captured at order time |
| `totalAmount` | number | ✅ | `>= 0` |
| `shippingAddress` | object | ❌ | `street`, `city`, `state`, `zip`, `country` |
| `paymentMethod` | enum | ❌ | `card` \| `cod` \| `paypal` — default `cod` |
| `paymentStatus` | enum | ❌ | Default `pending` |
| `status` | enum | ❌ | Default `pending` |
| `user` | ObjectId | ❌ | **Admins only** — place an order on someone's behalf. Ignored for customers, who are always bound to their own token id. |

### Responses

**201 Created**
```json
{
  "message": "Order created successfully",
  "order": {
    "_id": "66f3...",
    "user": "66f0...",
    "items": [{ "product": "66f2...", "quantity": 1, "price": 1499.99 }],
    "totalAmount": 1499.99,
    "status": "pending",
    "paymentStatus": "pending",
    "paymentMethod": "cod"
  }
}
```

| Status | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `401` | No token |
| `400` | Validation error — empty `items`, missing `totalAmount`, `quantity < 1`, or an invalid enum value |

> **Note:** `price` and `totalAmount` are taken from the request as-is; the server does not recompute them from the product catalogue, and stock is not decremented.

`🔒 Authenticated` — admins can update any order; customers only their own.

| Field | admin | customer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | ✅ | 🚫 stripped from the payload |

| `paymentMethod` | ✅ | 🚫 stripped |
| `shippingAddress` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `items`, `totalAmount` | ✅ | ✅ |

Disallowed fields are silently removed rather than rejected — a customer sending `status` still gets a `200`, but nothing changes.

### Example (customer-safe body)
```json
{
  "shippingAddress": { "city": "Lahore", "country": "Pakistan" }
}
```

# Bano Qabil 5.0 — E-Commerce Backend API

REST API for the MERN e-commerce project (Express 5 + Mongoose + JWT).

---

## Base URL

All requests use the `{{base_url}}` environment variable.

| Environment | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Local | `http://localhost:5000` |

The port comes from `PORT` in `backend/.env` (defaults to `3000` if unset).

## Authentication

The API uses **JWT Bearer tokens**.

1. Call **Auth → Login**. The saved test script automatically stores the returned JWT into the `{{token}}` environment variable.
2. Every other protected request inherits `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` from the collection-level auth — nothing else to do.

Token payload: `{ id, email, role }` · Expiry: **7 days** · Signed with `JWT_SECRET`.

## Roles

| Role | Capabilities |
| --- | --- |
| `customer` | Own profile, own orders, read products & categories |
| `admin` | Everything, plus user management and product/category writes |

## Standard error responses

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | Validation failure / duplicate record |
| `401` | Missing, malformed or expired token |
| `403` | Authenticated but role or ownership check failed |
| `404` | Resource not found |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded |
| `500` | Unhandled server error |

Error body is always: `{ "message": "..." }`

## Rate limiting

**100 requests per 15 minutes per IP**, applied globally. Responses include the standard `RateLimit-*` headers. Exceeding it returns `429` with the plain-text body `Too many requests from this IP, please try again later.`

## File uploads

Image uploads use `multipart/form-data` through Multer.

- Images only (`image/*` mimetype), max **5 MB** per file
- Saved to `backend/uploads/`, stored in Mongo as a relative path such as `/uploads/68f3...c1.png`
- Served publicly at `{{base_url}}/uploads/<filename>`

## Quick start

1. Select the **bano-qabil-local** environment (top-right of Postman).
2. Start the server: `npm run dev` inside `backend/`.
3. Run **Auth → Register (Admin)**, then **Auth → Login** — the token is captured automatically.
4. Everything else is ready to send.

## Error contract

Every error response — including 404s for unknown routes — is produced by one central handler and always has this shape:

```json
{ "message": "..." }
```

| Cause | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Malformed ObjectId (`CastError`) | `400` — `Invalid _id: <value>` |
| Schema validation failure | `400` — all failing fields, comma-separated |
| Duplicate unique field | `400` — `<field> already exists` |
| Malformed JSON body | `400` — `Invalid JSON body` |
| Missing/invalid/expired JWT | `401` |
| Role or ownership check | `403` |
| Unknown route | `404` — `Route not found - <METHOD> <path>` |
| Unhandled bug | `500` — generic message in production |
